title: Pair Up to Lower the Heaviest Pair
statement:
You get an array weights of even length. Split all of its elements into pairs, so that every element is in exactly one pair.

A pair's load is the sum of its two elements. Choose the pairing that makes the largest load as small as possible, and return that largest load.

examples.why: Pair 1 with 8 and 3 with 6: loads 9 and 9. Pairing neighbours after sorting, (1, 3) and (6, 8), gives 14.
There is only one way to pair two elements.

constraints: 2 ≤ weights.length ≤ 100 000, and the length is even
hints: Sort the array. The biggest element has to be paired with someone. Who is the safest partner?
The largest element should take the smallest one: any other partner is at least as big, so its pair can only get heavier.
After that pair is fixed, the same argument applies to what is left. So pair the i-th smallest with the i-th largest and take the biggest sum.

explain.intuition:
Think about the heaviest element M. Whoever it pairs with, that pair's load is at least M + partner. The smallest possible partner is the minimum element m, so giving M anything else can only hurt.

Is it ever bad for the rest? Suppose an optimal pairing has (M, x) and (m, y). Swap to (M, m) and (x, y). Now M + m ≤ M + x, and x + y ≤ M + x because y ≤ M. So the largest load does not grow. Repeat on the remaining elements: after sorting, pair from both ends inward.
steps: Put lo at the start and hi at the end.
While lo < hi, update the answer with weights[lo] + weights[hi], then move both pointers inward.
pitfalls: Pairing neighbours after sorting. That puts the two largest values together.
Returning the sum of the outermost pair only. In [1, 60, 60, 99] the middle pair (60, 60) is the heavier one.
Sorting numbers in JavaScript with plain sort(), which compares them as strings.

solutions.title: Try every pairing
solutions.idea: Pair the first unpaired element with each other one in turn and recurse. Exponential, only for tiny arrays.

solutions.title: Sort and pair the ends
solutions.idea: Smallest with largest, second smallest with second largest, and so on. An exchange argument shows no pairing does better.

followups: Values are at most 100 000. Can you avoid the comparison sort?
Form groups of three instead of pairs. Does the same greedy still work?
